title: applied-ml-weekly-notes-2026-03-03
content:
Weekly Applied ML research notes — March 3, 2026

Attendees: Ava Patel (owner), Liam Chen, Sofia Martinez, Ethan Brown, Priya Kapoor, guest: Dr. Mira Singh (external consultant)

Context and goals:
- Focus this week: finalize PTQ/GPTQ baseline comparisons, validate AWQ on LLaMA-3-8B variant, and stabilize onboarding checklist for Mistral-Next models.
- Primary success metric: end-to-end latency (p50/p95) and CPU/GPU memory footprint for 4-bit and 8-bit quantized variants, plus relative eval quality (ROUGE/EM/hallucination rate) within 2-3% of FP16 baseline.

Standups / async updates:
- Ava: ran GPTQ conversion pipeline on llama3-8b v1.2 on node-gpu-24. Observed inference memory decreased from 23GB to 6.1GB for 4-bit GPTQ; p95 latency increased by ~18% vs FP16 under batch size=1. Next: test KV-cache warmstart behavior.
- Liam: AWQ implementation (ours) produces smaller memory footprint than default GPTQ for some kernels; however token-by-token quality dips on commonsense QA dataset (ANLI dev) — investigating quantization paramization (block size, group size).
- Sofia: automated eval harness extended with hallucination metrics (QA-answer faithfulness classifier + n-gram overlap). Ran full eval on summarization suite (XSum+CNN/DailyMail) against FP16 and int4 variants. Preliminary: ROUGE-L drop ~1.8% for AWQ-int4, GPTQ-int4 drop ~2.5%.
- Ethan: tokenizer mismatch found during Mistral-Next onboarding (bpe special tokens mapping). Added conversion step in dockerized onboarding tool; filed PR to include token mapping table.
- Priya: started integration tests for dedicated-serving pipeline. Discovered a failure when using quantized models with dynamic batching + prefix caching; likely a KV cache alignment issue.

Meeting notes / experiments run:
1) GPTQ vs AWQ baseline (LLama3-8B, checkpoints: v1.1/v1.2)
- Configs: GPTQ 4-bit (g128), GPTQ 8-bit, AWQ 4-bit (group-size=128/block=64), AWQ 8-bit
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100-40GB (node-gpu-24), RTX6000 for dev
- Metrics captured: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, GPU memory (GB), ROUGE, EM, hallucination-rate, perplexity
- Results summary (high level):
  - Memory: int4 ~= 6-7GB, int8 ~= 12-13GB
  - Latency: int4 +15–25% p95 vs FP16, int8 +5–10%
  - Quality: AWQ-int4 less quality drop on summarization (ROUGE-L -1.8%) vs GPTQ-int4 (-2.5%) on same seed
  - Action: move AWQ-int4 into canary for summarization workloads; GPTQ-int4 for high throughput where slight quality loss acceptable.

2) KV-cache / dynamic batching bug
- Repro: quantized-llama3-8b + dynamic-batch=auto + prefix-cache enabled -> mismatch in next-token probabilities after 2nd token on ~3% of sequences
- Hypothesis: packing logic assumes FP16 cache layout; quantized kernels reorder cache entries or use different stride
- Owner: Priya + Liam to instrument cache layout and add alignment tests
- Deadline: 2026-03-10 for root cause or mitigation (fallback to FP16 for cached paths)

3) Eval harness improvements
- Added hallucination classifier (binary) trained on 1.2k annotated examples (internal dataset: AM-hallucination-1k)
- New dashboards for per-route evals (console): perplexity, ROUGE, hallucination-rate, latency overlay
- Next: add human-in-the-loop sampling for flagged regressions (Sofia to prototype)

4) Model onboarding checklist (Mistral-Next & LLaMA-3 variants)
- Steps added:
  - Checkpoint conversion (hf/torch -> internal fmt) + verify param sums
  - Tokenizer mapping + special tokens test (E2E tokenization on 50k synthetic prompts)
  - Compile with kernel-selector tests (small/medium/long sequence) and verify kernel fallback coverage
  - Run quick eval: QA dev (SQuAD v1), Summarization (XSum subset), Safety probes (internal safety-suite)
  - Observability hooks: per-token latency tracing, model-level cost estimate, quantization metadata in model manifest
- Owner for onboarding flow: Ethan (primary), Ava (review)

Action items (owners, due):
- Priya: instrument KV-cache alignment tests + start hotfix branch (due 2026-03-10)
- Liam: run AWQ parameter sweep (group-size 32/64/128, block 64/128) and submit results (due 2026-03-09)
- Sofia: schedule human eval sampling + implement feedback capture UI in eval harness (due 2026-03-17)
- Ethan: land tokenizer mapping PR + add CI tokenization tests (PR #3456) (due 2026-03-08)
- Ava: create canary rollout plan for AWQ-int4 summarization route (include rollback windows and SLOs) (due 2026-03-12)

Risks / blockers:
- Quantized kernel stability on older GPU drivers (470.x) — need to decide minimum driver in Dedicated documentation
- Onboarding docs incomplete for Mistral-Next: missing mapping for <|infill|> special tokens (tracked in JIRA-RED-1234)
- Eval suite compute cost: running full eval across 10 checkpoints is ~3x baseline cost; need signoff from infra budget owner

Notes / open questions:
- Should we standardize on AWQ as preferred int4 path? Tradeoffs: slightly better quality in summarization vs unknown corner-cases in QA. Need 2 weeks of canary data.
- Can we add an FP16 fallback only for cached-paths to avoid p95 regressions? Potentially acceptable as short-term mitigation.

References & links:
- PRs / tickets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/3421, https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/3456
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AM/quantization-experiments
